contribution_types.description:
Engineering: Generally, the accounts data are first serialized into bytecode before they are encoded into either base58 or base64, so the "gibberish" you are getting from the decoded base64 are the bytecode serialized data. You will then need to deserialize this bytecode into readable struct data. If you are building with anchor will also need to cut out the the first 8 byte as they are just discriminators and the remaining slice would be where the data lies in.

https://t.me/c/1615218389/1436

Engineering: If you're using anchor you can simply just leverage on their tools. Anchor uses borsh(https://github.com/near/borsh-rs) to serialise their data so you could use borsh directly too.

https://t.me/c/1615218389/1448

Engineering: Solana Programs can freely choose how they serialize and deserialize data within the block

Yup, the serialization and deserializastion are free to be specified, so it’s not necessary that programs use borsh. See https://docs.solana.com/developing/programming-model/transactions#instruction-data. For example look at how raydium does packing and unpacking of data. https://github.com/raydium-io/raydium-contract-instructions/blob/master/src/amm_instruction.rs#L278

https://t.me/c/1615218389/1452
